races.name: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns yearling, 180,000gns (breeze-up) 2yo; Havana Grey half-brother to 6f winner Top Biller (RPR 62); dam 5f scorer (including 2yo; 74), half-sister to 7f-1m2f Group 3 winner Mac Love; the biggest eye-catcher in terms of sales info among the newcomers; interesting.

runners_data.name: Californian Angel
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel and first foal of Listed-placed 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 102), from family of Lowther/Falmouth stakes winner Nahoodh; stable is operating at a good strike-rate with 2yos this term; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Lochryan
runners_data.spotlight: 52,000euros foal, £85,000 yearling; by Havana Grey; dam 1m2f winner (RPR 74), out of 5f 2yo winner, from family of champion sprinter Lochsong; stable had a winning 2yo newcomer at this course on Sunday; one to bear in mind.

runners_data.name: Primal
runners_data.spotlight: 70,000gns yearling; Starspangledbanner half-brother to winners Unassuming (1m/8.6f; RPR 99) and Bacchanalian (useful 2m hurdle), out of 1m AW scorer (73); not a pedigree pick but represents major yard.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.spotlight: £90,000 yearling; Blackbeard half-brother to Italian 1m 2yo winner Monte Vista, out of maiden (RPR 63) half-sister to Group-placed 6f 2yo/7f scorer Kitty Kiernan; suitably bred but stable is 0-7 with 2yos this term.

runners_data.name: Hadlan
runners_data.spotlight: 30,000euros yearling, 38,000gns (breeze-up) 2yo; Invincible Spirit half-brother to two winners, notably James McHenry (1m; RPR 100); dam 1m4f AW scorer (66), half-sister to 5f/5.5f 2yo Group 2 winner Gutaifan; market helpful.

runners_data.name: La Fuerza
runners_data.spotlight: 80,000euros yearling; by Churchill and first foal of French Listed-placed 7f winner (RPR 105) whose siblings include 7f 2yo scorer Blending, from family of Kingman; notable yard's second 2yo runner of the campaign.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Etoile
runners_data.spotlight: Best to forgive his last of nine at Pontefract (6f) where a slipped bit caused him to hang right throughout and prove difficult for his rider to control; better effort should be on the cards.

runners_data.name: True Charm
runners_data.comment: March foal by Ardad; £15,000 yearling, 25,000gns breeze-up 2yo; requires a market check
runners_data.spotlight: Showed clear promise with keeping-on second of 12, behind a fellow newcomer, in Windsor maiden (6f, good to firm); the form pick, albeit faces a couple of rivals who could be open to greater progress.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.comment: Yard had a first-time-out 2yo winner last weekend; respected if betting vibes strong
runners_data.spotlight: 110,000euros yearling purchase who is from a precocious family; performed well below market expectations (7-2 joint-favourite) in 6f contest at the York Dante festival, finishing down the field, but should be capable of much better; similar type to Menhaal.

runners_data.name: Menhaal
runners_data.spotlight: 260,000gns yearling purchase who is by a very smart 6f performer (including as a 2yo) for his connections; only seventh of ten when 10-11 favourite for Newbury maiden over this trip but showed signs of greenness and may well take a big step forward with the experience under his belt.

runners_data.name: Trust Yourself
runners_data.spotlight: Finished last of ten in 6f event at Ascot, living up to market expectations (rank outsider); best watched unless the signals from the betting go the other way.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Queen Of Christmas
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 305,000euros yearling; by Mehmas; ninth foal; half-sister to five winners including Wasmya (6f/7f including Listed; RPR 106), Wahdan (Group-placed French 9.5f AW; 105) and Talbah (Group-placed 7f; 104); dam 6.5f winner, out of half-sister to Arc winner Dylan Thomas; well related and she's respected on debut for a yard that has won the last three renewals of this.

runners_data.name: Senorita Bonita
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; 900,000gns breeze-up purchase; by Starspangledbanner; first foal; unraced dam closely related to winners Sub Rose (1m4f Group 3) and Astonishing (1m4f Listed), granddaughter of 1m Group 2 winner; was the top lot at this year's Craven breeze-up sale and she's interesting on debut.

runners_data.name: Terminology
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 95,000gns foal, 105,000gns yearling, 360,000euros breeze-up 2yo; by Havana Grey; third foal; half-sister to winners Pellitory (7f including 2yo; RPR 102) and Jalaybee (1m AW; 76); dam Listed-placed 5f AW 2yo winner (84); dam won on her debut and there's lots to like on debut for a yard that does well with 2yos.

runners_data.name: Delighfully Hot
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; filly by Too Darn Hot; second foal; dam 5f AW winner (including 2yo; RPR 85), closely related to 6f 2yo winner El Hadeeyah, out of 6f Listed winning half-sister to Listed-placed winners Rising Talent (1m-1m2f) and Laurentina (6f/7f 2yo); watch the betting on debut.

runners_data.name: Dreams Galore
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; by Havana Grey; first foal; dam 5f/6f winner (including Listed; RPR 103), half-sister to winners Romantic Style (7f Group 3) and Town And Country (5f Listed), out of French 7f 2yo Group 3 winner; speedy pedigree and she's one to note in the market on debut.

runners_data.name: Halliwell Stream
runners_data.comment: 140,000gns yearling; first foal of a Group-placed 5f 2yo winnner; a newcomer of note
runners_data.spotlight: Dam Group-placed 2yo winner (RPR 92); showed some speed but didn't quite see it out when fourth of ten on her debut at Yarmouth (5f, good; 8-1) two weeks ago; open to progress.

runners_data.name: Miss Tuite
runners_data.comment: Bred to be speedy and her stable is already off the mark with its 2yos
runners_data.spotlight: Dam placed five times on the AW over 6f; looked green early on her debut at Thirsk (5f, good; 28-1) 18 days ago but then got the hang of things and shaped well, finishing second of ten; that sets the standard but faces some nicely bred newcomers.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.comment: Attractively bred, by Blue Point out of a 6f 2yo winner (on debut) for her owner
runners_data.spotlight: Dam Group-placed 6f 2yo winner (RPR 97); 16-1 when third of eight on her debut at Goodwood (5f, good) 12 days ago, showing plenty of ability amidst greenness; open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Miss U Gino
runners_data.spotlight: Showed up well before weakening into fifth of seven on her debut at Newmarket (6f, good; 25-1) 18 days ago; drops in trip with better needed.

runners_data.name: My Normandie
runners_data.comment: 22-1 and no real impact (5f, good to firm) on her debut a fortnight ago; goes up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Seventh of ten on debut at Leicester (5f, good to firm) but showed a bit more when fifth of 12 at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 11 days ago; drop back in trip may not suit and likely she's one for further down the line.

races.name: Wildwest Beer Festival 4th July Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Safe Harbor
runners_data.note: Prominent racer improving with cheekpieces, David Egan booking suggests stable confidence after 19-day break
runners_data.spotlight: Third of five on her handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) last month and ran well in first-time cheekpieces when second of 13 at Newmarket (1m, good; third has won since) 19 days ago; respected with headgear retained.

runners_data.name: Bami
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 175-day absence, needs this tactical setup but freshness question remains
runners_data.comment: Consistent in four starts late last year, including winning a novice over C&D; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Won a novice on the AW at Lingfield (7f) in November and posted a solid effort on her handicap debut at Kempton (7f, AW) in December; off since and now steps up in trip with a hood applied on this switch back to turf; broke out of stalls and withdrawn at Lingfield last month (18-1 at the time).

runners_data.name: Jamie Sommers
runners_data.note: Proven at this course and distance, Laura Pearson's 0/19 record for trainer David Loughnane concerning
runners_data.comment: In a consistent vein of form; possibilities if taking well to first-time headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on to finish third of ten over this C&D in April and shaped as if still in good form at Windsor (1m, good to firm) next time; disappointed in first-time blinkers here 15 days ago but may bounce back with the headgear removed.

runners_data.name: Mayfair Market
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with tongue-tie added, Tom Marquand ride suggests each-way claims at decent odds
runners_data.comment: Showed some ability in four starts last year without progressing; tongue-tie on
runners_data.spotlight: Ran to a similar level in four starts last year (6f-1m); failed to make an instant impact in handicaps at Kempton (7f, AW; first-time tongue-tie) in May, having been held up off a steady pace; steps back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Lillie Margot
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner seeking to lead again, 25-day gap since promising second here ideal
runners_data.comment: Unexposed filly but she needs a transformation on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress in novice/maiden events but showed improved form when second of seven over this C&D (good) on her handicap debut 25 days ago; ridden positively that day and she's a contender.

runners_data.name: Vitality
runners_data.note: Front-runner prone to doing too much early, Jack Callan's 3lb claim helpful but inexperience shows
runners_data.comment: Placed in pair of novices at Southwell and Epsom last month so can't be ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who is unraced on ground slower than good; ran to a similar level on her first two starts but did too much too soon before weakening at Bath (1m, firm) three weeks ago; may bounce back on her handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Prominent runner improving in handicaps, Cieren Fallon booking significant positive
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten around 8l when third of 12 in a maiden at Newcastle (1m, AW) in April and ran with credit when second of four on her handicap debut at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) 29 days ago; hung right that day and cheekpieces are added for her first start on turf.

runners_data.name: Laughterintherain
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, 38-day break may have freshened her up
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off favourite when disappointing on her debut at Newmarket in October but it was an improved effort when second of 12 in a novice at Lingfield (7f, AW) in December; ran to a similar level when behind a couple of these on her handicap debut over this C&D in April and she may come on for that first start for 139 days.

runners_data.name: Morningtoncrescent
runners_data.note: Consistent but limited hold-up type, headgear changes suggest stable trying to find improvement
runners_data.comment: 150-1 and on toes when sixth at Newbury three weeks ago; this race looks too tough
runners_data.spotlight: Sixth in each of her three starts, with the best of those efforts coming at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; disappointed at Chester (1m4f, good) 26 days ago and now makes her handicap debut over the shortest trip she's attempted in first-time cheekpieces; improvement needed.

runners_data.name: Glasgow Kiss
runners_data.note: Disappointing hold-up horse despite Oisin Murphy booking, visor first-time may help concentration
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced filly but she was tailed off on handicap debut at Bath (1m) last month
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in a novice at Southwell on her stable debut in February but she's failed to build on that in three starts since; failed to beat a rival here 25 days ago and now has a visor added.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: Front-runner with blinkers fitted, Lewis Edmunds needs to judge pace better than last effort
runners_data.comment: Chance largely depends on the effects of new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off at Lingfield (1m, AW) in April but she ran better in first-time blinkers over this C&D (good to soft) 15 days ago; needs to build on that.

races.paceDynamic: Vitality, Lillie Margot and Katalyst will all attempt to lead this 11-runner fillies' handicap, creating a strong gallop from the start over this extended 1m2f trip. The three confirmed front-runners will likely engage early, with Safe Harbor and Mimi's Magic sitting prominent behind the pace battle. This sustained gallop will test stamina reserves and set up a finish that strongly favours hold-up horses like Bami, Jamie Sommers, and Morningtoncrescent who can finish off a truly-run race. The early pace pressure clearly benefits closers over prominent racers in this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders (Vitality, Lillie Margot, Katalyst) go forward and create genuine pace pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will exhaust the early pace-setters and allow patient hold-up horses to pick up the pieces in the final two furlongs. Fresh finishers with tactical speed will thrive off this honest pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If one leader drops out early leaving just two to set a more manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: Without maximum pace pressure, the prominent horses can travel comfortably and use their position to advantage when the race develops. Safe Harbor and Mimi's Magic are perfectly placed to capitalise on this rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lillie Margot Dominates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Vitality and Katalyst both miss the break or settle, leaving Lillie Margot with an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: She gets the perfect front-running scenario over her proven course and distance, controlling the gallop to suit her stamina. Her previous second place here gives her a significant tactical edge in this situation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go too hard early and completely capitulate in the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between whatever horses have been held up furthest back with the most energy reserves. This extreme scenario rewards only the most patiently ridden runners.

watchPoints.text: Vitality and Katalyst both going too fast early and taking each other out of the race completely
Safe Harbor and Mimi's Magic getting trapped behind the early pace battle if leaders spread across track
Jamie Sommers getting the perfect hold-up position if pace develops as expected given her course form
Bami showing ring-rustiness early after 175-day absence despite fitting tactical profile
Lillie Margot getting isolated in front if other two leaders settle behind her unexpectedly

races.name: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Oisin Murphy aboard who needs luck in running from this crowded finish
runners_data.comment: Narrowly ahead of Beach Point when placed both starts this term; tight between them again
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 but he's finished in the first three on 11 occasions, including in each of his three starts this year; beaten a neck here over 8.5f last summer and he's a solid contender once again.

runners_data.name: Abando
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 111-day break, gelded since last run but faces strong pace bias
runners_data.comment: Group form in Germany; gelding operation/h'cap debut/mark in freefall so watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-German; well held in two maidens for Marco Botti last year and a similar story in two novice events for this stable; gelded since last seen in February and has cheekpieces back on for his handicap debut, so he's worth keeping an eye on in the betting.

runners_data.name: Caph Star
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner in April, needs to overcome hold-up style disadvantage but has winning form here
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 7yo; beat 13 others (1m2f) in April; creditable third (1m3f) latest; player
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on ground slower than good; off the mark for this yard when winning over C&D in April and he ran another solid race when third of ten at Kempton (1m3f, AW) next time; however, he was reported to have ran flat at Newmarket 19 days ago and needs to bounce back; hood removed.

runners_data.name: Star Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for in-form Alan King yard, dead-heated last time but running style works against race shape
runners_data.comment: May need a stiffer test than this now, but market useful nonetheless after 433 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Dead-heated at Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW) in November 2024 and he was runner-up over that C&D last February; showed he retains ability when fifth at Kempton (1m3f, AW) on his first start for 433 days last month and may come on for it, although this drop back in trip may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should get ideal position tracking Orangesandlemons and avoid late traffic
runners_data.comment: Four AW wins since December; return to 1m can help but no easy task off revised mark
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins on the AW in Class 6 company since December (6f-8.5f); respectable efforts on his last two outings but he possibly didn't quite get home over this trip at Ripon last month; each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Another prominent type stepping up in trip, tactical position suits but needs improvement
runners_data.comment: Eight-race maiden and he needs a transformation at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8; placed in a maiden here last June but he's been well held in six starts since, five of which were handicaps; steps up in trip with better needed; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Orangesandlemons
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner, dual winner who should get uncontested lead to exploit
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winner, with the most recent success coming over 8.5f here in October (good to soft); solid reappearance at Wolverhampton in April but was well held here 25 days ago (trainer's rep said she would prefer an easier surface); steps up in trip and she's a contender if the ground is slower than good.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing blinkers for first time, recent wind surgery but faces tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Held on his AW comeback from wind surgery three weeks ago but entitled to come on for that
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winner for Jane Chapple-Hyam but has been quite disappointing since the latest of those wins; held in two starts since undergoing wind surgery and blinkers are now tried instead of cheekpieces; down another 3lb.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose wins came on softer ground, needs to overcome good going concerns
runners_data.comment: Off seven months but has gone well fresh before; each-way possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have been over 1m2f on good to soft, with the most recent coming at Doncaster in September after the first past the post was disqualified for a banned substance; well beaten at Newbury on his return but this is a drop in grade.

runners_data.name: Kasgani
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well on stable debut 46 days ago but style disadvantage in crowded finish
runners_data.comment: A new recruit for Declan Carroll; the betting should help guide to expectations
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 in Ireland for Dermot Weld but he caught the eye on his stable debut over C&D 46 days ago, staying on for third behind Caph Star having been denied a clear run; that was his first start since October and this unexposed gelding is on the shortlist.

races.paceDynamic: Orangesandlemons is the sole identified front runner and will likely get an uncontested lead with No Knee Never and Give Me The Night providing some early company in prominent positions. The bulk of this field are hold-up horses (A Major Payne, Abando, Caph Star, Star Time, Primo Lara, Kasgani) who will settle behind the pace. With minimal early pressure, Orangesandlemons can dictate fractions and kick for home, while the large hold-up contingent will face a traffic-laden finish as they all look for racing room simultaneously. This race shape strongly favours the early pace-setters and prominent racers who can avoid the late scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Orangesandlemons gets soft fractions and isn't headed turning for home.
scenarios.body: The pace-setter can dictate terms without pressure and has enough in reserve to hold off late challengers who get caught in traffic. Prominent racers like No Knee Never benefit from clean runs while hold-up horses struggle for room.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If No Knee Never or Give Me The Night track the leader closely and strike at the right moment.
scenarios.body: These horses get perfect trips behind the uncontested leader and can time their challenges to perfection while the hold-up brigade gets tangled up behind them. The winner comes from just off the pace with a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and multiple hold-up horses find clear runs.
scenarios.body: One of the many hold-up horses like A Major Payne or Caph Star gets a dream passage through the field as others get stopped. The winner needs both class and luck to navigate the congested finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Orangesandlemons goes too fast early or gets headed before the turn.
scenarios.body: The front runner cracks under unexpected pressure from prominent runners, creating a sprint finish that suits horses with tactical speed. Late runners get their preferred scenario but still need clear runs.

watchPoints.text: Orangesandlemons breaks too fast early and burns up energy that allows prominent runners to close
Traffic problems developing in home straight as multiple hold-up horses look for racing room simultaneously
No Knee Never tracking the leader closely and measuring his run to strike at optimal moment
A Major Payne and other hold-up horses getting shuffled back further as pace quickens
Something Splendid handling the good ground better than recent form suggests on softer surfaces

races.name: Watch RacingTV Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won well at Ripon 39 days ago but faces much stronger opposition here making handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise on debut at Wolverhampton in March and built on that at Ripon (1m2f, good) 39 days ago, coming clear with the runner-up to win a maiden; that form is ordinary but she should have more to offer in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Gatehouse
runners_data.note: Reliable hold-up performer but hung left badly last time and may struggle to overcome poor draw if gets one
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins before put firmly in his place on turf debut at Newmarket (good to firm)
runners_data.spotlight: Won on the AW at Chelmsford (1m2f) in December and followed up on his handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) in April; however, he hung left and was well held on his turf debut at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) 31 days ago; this is a drop in grade.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.comment: Gelded since latest 1m2f effort; drop in trip looks worth exploring
runners_data.spotlight: Ran to a similar level in two starts over 1m2f in April but was below that level when a never-dangerous eighth of ten over 8.5f here 15 days ago; that was his first start since being gelded and he may do better now stepping back up in trip on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Midnight Rodeo
runners_data.note: Only natural front runner who should get uncontested lead but carries 7lb more than last win
runners_data.comment: Ended 2yo campaign on the up; 7lb higher in a stronger race but returns with yard in form
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for a step up in trip and switch to nurseries last year, winning at Kempton (1m, AW) and Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) in September; 7lb higher than for that latest success and needs to take a step forward from last month's reappearance at Windsor.

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: Raced too freely at Hamilton but if settles better can track the leader and get first run
runners_data.spotlight: Showed ability in novice company but no immediate impact in handicaps when down the field at Hamilton (8.5f, good) 19 days ago; raced freely that day and will need to settle better over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Barbury Boy
runners_data.note: Won well at Beverley but failed to settle over 1m4f last time, so this trip reduction should help
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improved form when winning at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm; runner-up has won twice since) in April but he didn't settle at Haydock (1m4f, good) 25 days ago; this drop back in trip could suit and he's open to further progress.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Improved significantly last time at Yarmouth but still needs to prove he can win a race
runners_data.comment: 40-1 and 125-1 when last at Newmarket (1m) in October and Nottingham (1m2f) recently
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival on his first two starts (1m/1m2f) but showed much more at a huge price when fifth of nine at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) 34 days ago; gelded since and this step back up in trip should suit on his handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Rodeo is the only confirmed front runner in this seven-runner field and should get an uncontested lead over this 1m2f trip. With most rivals being hold-up performers (Mudita, Gatehouse, Barbury Boy, That Darn Cantor) and only Unchartedterritory likely to race prominently, the early pace will be moderate to steady. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to Midnight Rodeo, as the lack of early pace pressure will allow the leaders to dictate terms and kick clear in the straight before the hold-up horses can mount their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Rodeo gets an easy lead and dictates the fractions
scenarios.body: The Scott runner will be able to quicken off steady fractions and prove difficult to peg back over this stamina-testing trip. The hold-up horses will have too much ground to make up in the straight against a horse who has won from the front twice before.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Time Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of Mudita and Barbury Boy will pay dividends as they can unleash late runs. Both have shown good finishing kicks when getting the right pace scenario and stronger jockeys will be crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Unchartedterritory settles better and tracks Midnight Rodeo
scenarios.body: The O'Meara runner can get first run on the leader while staying out of trouble. His previous free-running style becomes an asset if he can position just behind the pace and pounce approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Rodeo goes too slowly and gets swamped late
scenarios.body: The superior class of Barbury Boy and Mudita tells as they sweep past tired leaders. This becomes a pure stamina test where the highest-rated horses with the strongest finishes prevail in a bunch finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Midnight Rodeo gets pressured early by Unchartedterritory as neither will want to give the other an easy time
Monitor Unchartedterritory's early behaviour after racing too freely last time at Hamilton
Check if Barbury Boy settles better dropped back to 1m2f after failing to stay 1m4f at Haydock
Observe if any hold-up horses get trapped behind the small field as there will be limited cover
Watch for trouble in running with several hold-up horses needing luck in a small field with limited racing room

races.name: Dine In Sherwoods Restaurant Handicap

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who needs pace to aim at, returns from 27-day break with respectable Windsor form
runners_data.comment: Not built on her 2yo debut effort, but drops to Class 6 company on her seasonal return
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden but she has posted some respectable efforts, including when fifth of eight at Windsor (6f, good to firm) on her reappearance last month; dropped another 2lb.

runners_data.name: Ishe Worth Agamble
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with proven course form, Tim Easterby 12/103 record boosts confidence
runners_data.comment: Did well last year; just a respectable third last month but might come on for the run
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times last season, the most recent coming at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) in July; respectable third over this C&D on his return in April and kept on for fifth of 11 at Redcar (6f, good) 16 days ago; contender if things drop right.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf after 113-day absence, distance drop from 5f wins is questionable
runners_data.spotlight: Last five wins have been over 5f, the most recent at Wolverhampton (AW) in December; below best in four starts since and now returns to turf for the first time since October 2024 folllowing a 113-day break.

runners_data.name: Jake Loves Laura
runners_data.note: Prominent 15-race maiden carrying just 122lbs, recent Chelmsford third suggests improvement
runners_data.spotlight: 15-race maiden but ran one of her better races for this yard when a 2l third of seven at Chelmsford (6f, AW) in February; however, she was disappointing in a classified event 95 days ago and has been off since.

runners_data.name: Hint Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with recent 6f form, tactical advantage of uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins in February and he went close at Southwell last week; respected back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on the AW over 7f in February and has gone close on his last two starts, including over this trip 28 days ago; has form on turf and this prominent-racer has claims.

runners_data.name: Run This Way
runners_data.note: In-form prominent runner with recent double under blinkers, good going suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: Comfy win in new blinkers at Redcar nine days ago; 3lb rise still leaves her competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Had blinkers on for the first time when winning at Redcar (6f, good; has won on soft) last month and followed up at Thirsk (6f, good) 18 days ago, beating 16 rivals; back up another 7lb but can't be dismissed in her bid for the hat-trick.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 18-day turnaround, hasn't built on promising stable debut form
runners_data.comment: Below last August's last winning mark but not at the top of her game on last five starts
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times for Ollie Sangster (5.5f/6f); solid effort when beaten only 2l at Wolverhampton on her stable debut in December but she's not built on that in two starts since; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Course winner returning from quiet spell, 12-day break since Bath effort with cheekpieces off
runners_data.comment: Just 1-14 but she's on a reduced mark and her win came after an absence; new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner on stable debut last April (good to firm) but quiet at the end of 2025; fair fifth of 12 at Bath (5.5f, good to firm; first-time cheekpieces replaced blinkers) on reappearance; needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Non-runner status confirmed, 99-day absence would have been concern anyway
runners_data.comment: Placed three times from eight starts over this C&D, but is on a losing run of 38
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins over 6f at Wolverhampton (in some form of headgear) but was placed on turf on multiple occasions in 2025; failed to beat a rival at Southwell in February, though, and headgear left off on first start since.

runners_data.name: Court Of Session
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose five wins came over further trips on AW surfaces
runners_data.spotlight: All five wins have been on the AW over further than this, the latest at Wolverhampton in January; below his best in three starts since finishing third there in February and he's 0-15 on turf.

runners_data.name: Tilsworth Turf
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades late pattern, 134-day absence makes him vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins came over 6f on soft ground in 2024 but he's mostly struggled since the latest of them; off for 134 days and he's best watched.

runners_data.name: Surprise Again
runners_data.note: Prominent type with fade tendency, massive 254-day layoff rules out winning chances
runners_data.spotlight: Poor form in five starts, including in two handicaps (6f/7f); absent for 254 days and much better is needed.

races.paceDynamic: Hint Of The Jungle will set a controlled pace from the front with Run This Way, Alafdhal, Jake Loves Laura, and Tilsworth Turf providing the early company in a race lacking genuine speed merchants. The pace will be honest but not breakneck, allowing the field to stay in touch through the first four furlongs before the real business begins inside the final two furlongs. With only one confirmed front-runner and several prominent racers who can adapt their position, this creates a tactical affair where positioning matters more than raw speed. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and late runners who can exploit what should be a sprint finish from the two-furlong marker.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Hint Of The Jungle sets an uncontested lead and the prominent runners settle kindly behind him.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a sprint from two furlongs out when the pace lifts, suiting horses with a turn of foot who can pick up the leaders. Hold-up specialists with proven finishing kicks will thrive in the dash to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Run This Way and Alafdhal press Hint Of The Jungle early, creating genuine pace pressure in the opening half-mile.
scenarios.body: The early gallop will stretch the field and set up the race for something with stamina to come from behind. Horses that need the pace to collapse will benefit as the early leaders weaken in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Hint Of The Jungle gets an easy time in front and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: His recent good form and tactical advantage of an uncontested lead allows him to build a decisive advantage. The hold-up horses will struggle to close the gap if he gets first run on them from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too slow and the field bunches up for a cavalry charge finish.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test in the final furlong where class and natural pace matter most. The highest-rated horses with tactical speed will emerge from the pack when it matters.
